title: sneed-and-feed/lean-theorems-1
abstract: A complete machine-checked Lean 4 formalization of Descartes's Rule of Signs (1637, Wiedijk #73). Proves that for any non-zero real polynomial p(X) over ℝ, the number of positive real roots counted with algebraic multiplicity is bounded above by the number of sign variations in its coefficient sequence (ignoring zero coefficients), and their difference is an even non-negative integer. While the pinned Mathlib revision (Mathlib v4.34.0-rc1) contains the upper-bound inequality in `Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.RuleOfSigns` (`Polynomial.roots_countP_pos_le_signVariations`), this development formalizes the complete two-part theorem by proving the even-parity conclusion (Gauss 1828), establishing the sign-variation parity correspondence with leading and trailing coefficients, and providing a direct list-based coefficient sequence interface.
